title.text: Slate is an infinite canvas for your study work. Write by hand, read papers beside your notes, and keep it all in your gym repository on GitHub.

live.text: It runs right in the browser, and installs on your iPad. We'll set it up at the end.

canvas.text: Part one: the canvas. Write with the Pencil, with real pressure.
Pick a colour and a size, or save them as a preset.
The highlighter stays behind your writing.
Erase whole strokes, or cut through part of one.
Text boxes understand Markdown and LaTeX maths, and a to-do is one tap to tick.
Every day starts with a dated line. Its label stays pinned as you pan, and the tag button files the day under your gym topics, like eigenvalues.
Take a photo of the board, right onto the canvas. Resize it, place it, and draw on it. When you move the photo, the ink moves with it.
Need room? The space tool pushes everything below it down.
Lasso anything: ink, text or images. Then move it, scale it, recolour it, or duplicate it.
Sketch a rough box and an arrow, and Beautify turns them into clean shapes. Restore brings your own ink back, any time.
Pinch to zoom. The minimap and the list of dates take you back to any day, and Home brings you back to today.
And everything can be undone, and redone.

paper.text: Part two: reading a paper. Import a PDF, and it opens beside the canvas.
Highlight a passage, circle something with the pen, or add a margin note. The PDF itself never changes.

paper.step: Lasso a figure onto the canvas
paper.text: Lasso a figure and send it to the canvas. It arrives as a clip, with its text, and a link back to the page.

paper.step: Source badge back to the page
paper.text: Tap the clip's badge, and the paper opens right at that spot, even offline.

chatbot.text: Part three: chatbot answers. Copy an answer, and paste it in, maths and all.

chatbot.step: Lasso part of it onto the canvas
chatbot.text: Lasso the part you need, and drag it onto the canvas. It links back to the answer.

chatbot.step: New from link: Reader and Original
chatbot.text: New from link saves a web article, through your own small fetch helper, as a clean reader view.
The original page is kept too, and it opens offline.

gym.text: Part four: marking for gym. Lasso some worked notes, and mark them for gym, as a note, a problem, a solution or a question, with a topic and a comment.
An agent in your gym repository formalizes the mark, and the flag becomes a badge that opens the gym file.

lookup.text: Part five: lookup and revision. Browse your whole gym repository, topics, notes and problems, rendered with maths, even offline.
Search all of gym; results open right at their section.
The revision list shows what to revisit next.
To-dos collects your checklist, and every to-do on your canvases. Tap one to jump to it.

panes.text: Part six: panes. Books, clippings and gym files open as tabs beside the canvas. Drag the divider, swap sides, or go full screen.
A second canvas can sit right beside the first.
EPUB books work too, with a table of contents, maths and highlights.
Changes save on the device first, and sync to gym.
Light or dark, as you like.
And it works offline. Changes wait, and sync when you're back.

phone.text: On a phone, the canvas and the side pane take turns. The layers button switches between them.
Lasso something in the side pane, and it waits in the carry tray. Switch to the canvas, and drag it to where it belongs.

setup.text: Part seven: setting up. Open Slate in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
On first run, Slate shows you how to make a fine-grained GitHub token, for your gym repository only.
Enter the repository, the branch, and the token.
Slate checks the token, then syncs for the first time.
Optionally, deploy the free fetch helper, and add it in Settings to save web pages.

end.text: Slate is at preetsingh-007.github.io/slate. Open it in Safari, add it to your Home Screen, and start writing.
